$comment: Source catalog. This is the single registry of every feed. Onboarding a source is an adapter module plus an entry here — no pipeline code change. Verified live 2026-08-07.

sources.$authComment: The token was COMMITTED HERE as a 64-character literal until a security review raised it, and is now in Secrets Manager like every other feed credential. It remains genuinely public - published in the federal ITS WorkZone Feed Registry (data.transportation.gov/resource/69qe-yiui), no signup, verified byte-identical to the registry value 2026-08-10 - so this is not a confidentiality fix. It is a fix for what the artifact TEACHES: a hardcoded credential in a reference architecture handed to state DOTs models the wrong pattern whatever the token's own sensitivity, and the ADR 0004 exception that excused it did not survive being read by someone who had not read the ADR. Populate with: aws secretsmanager create-secret --name corridor-event-hub/ok-odot-wzdx-token --secret-string "$(curl -s 'https://data.transportation.gov/resource/69qe-yiui.json?$limit=5000' | python3 -c 'import json,sys,urllib.parse as u;[print(u.parse_qs(u.urlsplit(r["url"]).query)["access_token"][0]) for r in json.load(sys.stdin) if r.get("issuingorganization")=="Oklahoma Department of Transportation"]')". Override locally with OK_ODOT_TOKEN. See ADR 0004.
sources.$authQueryParamComment: This feed spells its credential parameter `access_token`; TxDOT and AZ511 spell theirs `key`. The name is DATA rather than a per-source branch in the collector, which is what let this source move to api_key_secret without new code. Absent means `key`.

Unmappable values are recorded rather than dropped, so a steady rate is correct behaviour and only a spike means the format drifted. Drives the per-source CorridorEventHub-mapping-issue-spike-* alarm threshold; raise it if this feed legitimately gets noisier.
sources.$cadenceComment: DECLARED by the feed itself: road_event_feed_info.update_frequency = 60. This is the only source in the catalog whose number came from the publisher rather than from inference.
sources.$cadenceMeasured: MEASURED 2026-08-12 over 1,411 fetches / 23.5h: every payload byte-distinct, so the checksum method reports a 60s publish rate and PROVES NOTHING. The feed regenerates end_date as (request time + fixed offset) on every request - across a 84,598s gap, end_date advanced 84,598s on 54 of 57 records, a 1.0000 ratio. Consecutive polls differed in 61 values and ALL of them were end_date. The real publish cadence of the event content is still unmeasured, and cannot be measured from raw bytes on this feed - it needs a hash over the mapped fields with end_date excluded. See also the end_date note in `observed`.
sources.$snapshotComment: OPEN QUESTION 2 — CRITICAL. When a record disappears from this snapshot, does it mean CLEARED or UNKNOWN? Not answerable from the data. Requires a call to ODOT. Until confirmed the pipeline MUST treat disappearance as `unknown`, never `cleared` — the conservative failure.

end_date up to 2029 with millisecond precision — synthetic placeholder

end_date SLIDES: computed as (request time + fixed offset), so it advances with the clock and the zone never ends. Measured over a 84,598s gap, end_date advanced 84,598s on 54 of 57 records. Near-term dates (2026-10-19T22:16:48.354Z) are generated identically to the absurd ones (2029-08-05T22:16:48.351Z) and share a minute-of-day to the millisecond. The adapter rejects the whole cohort; 3 of 5 I-40 candidates lost a published end_time as a result. WORTH RAISING WITH ODOT.

sources.$interimComment: THIS SOURCE IS INTERIM. It exists because class 4 had no real-time option at all, not because it is the right long-term answer. Three limitations are properties of the tile SCHEMA and therefore unfixable in the adapter: (1) no confidence/provenance band, (2) no direction, (3) not redistributable. PLANNED REPLACEMENT: NPMRDS via RITIS for provenance/TMC referencing/historical baselines, and/or a commercial probe feed (INRIX, HERE direct, TomTom) for real-time WITH redistribution rights. When one lands, this entry becomes a corroborating source rather than the only source for congestion - and `time_confidence: estimated` plus `direction: UNKNOWN` in the adapter MUST be revisited, since both exist only because this feed cannot state them. Note HERE-direct would stay in independenceGroup `here`, so it does not add independence. See DATA-SOURCES.md, 'The replacement path for class 4'.
sources.$snapshotComment: Known, and the CONTRAST CASE to the state 511 feeds: a queue that disappears from the flow layer genuinely means the queue is gone, because flow is a continuous measurement rather than a report someone has to remember to retract. Same certainty as NWS, opposite of OK/TX/AZ.

notes: z8 corridor coverage: 17 tiles, 1,586 traffic_flow features + 59 traffic_incidents.
Live congestion present: 1,535 'free', 35 'minor', 5 'slow', 6 'queuing', 3 'stationary', 2 'none'.

NO CONFIDENCE FIELD. HERE's own API publishes bands saying whether a speed is observed, historical, or speed-limit-derived; the tile schema drops them. A speed here cannot be told apart from a historical average, so it must never corroborate an agency-reported closure on its own.

NO DIRECTION FIELD. Each carriageway is a separate feature but no heading is stated, so direction is UNKNOWN on every candidate. Biggest gap in this source: 'queue eastbound' and 'queue westbound' are different events to a truck.
NO PUBLISH TIMESTAMP on flow features. start_time/stop_time exist only on traffic_incidents (epoch seconds).
Stable numeric `id` per segment and incident - a real correlation key for the matcher across polling cycles, which no other source provides.
`congestion` is a 0-1 ratio and was 0.0 on nearly every free-flowing segment, so classification leans on `kind` rather than the ratio.
Segments are sub-tile fragments and the same id recurs in adjacent tiles; the adapter collapses repeats as tile bookkeeping, not as dedup.
Three layers: traffic_flow, traffic_incidents, and incident_icons (the same incidents as points for label placement - skipped, not data loss).

A direct HERE Traffic API adapter would share this group and the two MUST NOT corroborate each other - same upstream observations reaching us by two routes is not independent evidence, and treating it as such inflates confidence exactly when it should not.

sources.$corridorComment: BLOCKED ON A DECISION, not on engineering: config/corridor.json currently defines I-40 as 'western AZ border to eastern OK border' with AZ at corridorOffset 0. California I-40 (Barstow -> Needles, ~155 mi) is OUTSIDE that definition. Admitting CA means prepending a CA segment, and test_the_first_state_starts_at_corridor_zero forces CA to offset 0 - which RE-BASES every existing corridor measure by ~155 mi. Any measure already persisted becomes wrong. Decide re-base vs. negative-offset before wiring an adapter.

notes: RICHEST CLOSURE SCHEMA OF ANY SOURCE IN THIS CATALOG. Has begin AND end coordinates, begin/end postmile, begin/end milepost, county, elevation, travelFlowDirection, facility, typeOfClosure, typeOfWork, durationOfClosure, estimatedDelay, lanesClosed, totalExistingLanes, and separate request/start/end timestamps.

FIRST SOURCE WITH BOTH POSTMILE AND MILEPOST as distinct fields. Every other feed gives one or neither. Postmile is Caltrans' own LRS ('R22.620' - the R is an alignment PREFIX, not part of the number); milepost is the corridor-comparable one. Parsing postmile as a float silently drops the prefix and collides realigned segments.

LANES ARE NOT ALWAYS A NUMBER. lanesClosed observed as '1', '2', 'All', '1, 2', and 'RShoulder' on I-40. int() throws on three of five. 'RShoulder' means a shoulder closure, which is NOT a lane closure and must not decrement totalExistingLanes.

`index` IS a unique key (0 duplicates in 1275) and encodes closureID-logNumber-date-time. (closureID, logNumber) is NOT unique - 130 duplicate pairs, because the same log is reissued per time window. Keying on the pair collapses distinct closures.
TIMESTAMPS ARE TRIPLE-ENCODED: closureStartDate + closureStartTime + closureStartEpoch, all three present and redundant. Epoch is seconds. Prefer epoch; the date/time pair carries no zone.
isClosureEndIndefinite is an explicit boolean, true on 14 of 1275 - the first source that DECLARES an open-ended end rather than leaving it null (contrast NWS ends:null).

typeOfClosure vocabulary observed: Lane, Full. facility observed: Mainline, Conventional Hwy, On Ramp, Off Ramp, Rest Area. 'Conventional Hwy' on an I-40 record means the frontage/conventional segment, NOT the interstate mainline - filtering to Mainline changes the I-40 count substantially.
estimatedDelay is 'Not Reported' or a bare number of minutes as a string - no units field.

I-40 records cluster into a handful of real closures (C40BA, C40GA, C40KA, T40LA, T40VA) reissued across windows, so 32 records is NOT 32 distinct events - dedup applies WITHIN this source, before cross-agency matching.
Two I-40 rest-area full closures (T40VA) with isClosureEndIndefinite=true and Emergency Work - the only rest-area signal any feed on this corridor carries.

sources.$seedReliabilityComment: Highest of the state DOT feeds (above OK/TX/AZ at 0.8) because it is the operating agency's own closure-permit system with begin/end geometry and explicit lane counts, not a public-facing summary. Below NBI (0.9) because permits describe INTENT and a scheduled closure may not be in place yet.
sources.$independenceComment: ALL FOUR ca-cwwp2-* feeds share this group deliberately. They are four views from one District 8 TMC database, so an LCS closure and a CMS sign describing it are the SAME report reaching us twice - they MUST NOT corroborate each other. See also weathershare-oss, which re-serves this data.

sources.$specComment: The payload wrapper is Caltrans', but the FIELD NAMES AND UNITS ARE NTCIP 1204 ESS objects (essAirTemperature, essSurfaceStatus, essPrecipSituation). That is a real published standard, so unlike the other CWWP2 feeds there IS a spec to diff against - and the enumerations are normative, not guessable.
sources.$cadenceComment: recordTimestamp advanced ~15 min behind wall clock at probe time (13:45 vs 14:00). ASSUMED, measure before trusting.
sources.$snapshotComment: Sensor readings, not reports - a station dropping a value means the sensor stopped reporting, not that conditions cleared. Same certainty class as NWS and aws-location-traffic, opposite of the 511 feeds. NOTE the asymmetry: absence of a READING is UNKNOWN, but a reading of 'dry' is a real observation.
sources.$statusComment: Same two blockers as ca-cwwp2-lcs: no adapter, and the corridor definition excludes CA.

notes: THIS DOES NOT CLOSE CLASS 6 ON I-40, and that is the headline finding. Both I-40 stations report numEssPavementSensors=0 - no surface status, no surface temperature, no freeze point. The five D8 stations that DO have pavement sensors are on I-15, SR-2, SR-18 and SR-138 (mountain routes where chain control matters). I-40 is desert, so Caltrans instrumented it for wind and visibility, not ice.
So on I-40 this is a WEATHER source (air temp, wind, gust, humidity, visibility, precip) and NOT a road-surface source. The road_surface class stays derived, exactly as DATA-SOURCES.md says for NWS.

EVERY VALUE IS AN INTEGER IN NTCIP SCALED UNITS AND CARRIES NO UNIT FIELD. Verified against WeatherShare's decoding of the same station: essAirTemperature 381 = 38.1 C (tenths of a degree C, = 100.6 F); essAvgWindSpeed 50 = 5.0 m/s (tenths m/s, = 11.2 mph); essMaxWindGustSpeed 119 = 11.9 m/s; essVisibility 332700 = 33.27 km (DECIMETRES). Reading 381 as degrees or 332700 as metres is silently, enormously wrong.

essSurfaceStatus IS AN ENUM, NOT A MEASUREMENT: NTCIP 1204 gives other(1), error(2), dry(3), traceMoisture(4), wet(5), chemicallyWet(6), iceWarning(7), iceWatch(8), snowWarning(9), snowWatch(10), absorption(11), dew(12), frost(13), ice(14), glaze(15). Observed 1, 3 and 5 in D8. Treating it as ordinal severity is wrong - 1 is 'other', not 'least severe'.

SENTINEL/UNSET VALUES ARE INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM READINGS. essSurfaceTemperature observed as 0 (SR-138) and 1001 (I-15 at US-395, = 100.1 C, physically impossible for pavement) alongside plausible 273/373/392. essMinTemp 0 appears next to essMaxTemp 301. Absent fields use the STRING 'Not Reported', so a numeric parse must handle a non-numeric string too.
essTemperatureSensorTable CAN BE EMPTY - the I-15 Desert Oasis station has zero temperature sensors, so table[0] raises IndexError. Sensor tables are variable-length per station, not fixed.

essPavementSensorLocation packs a whole location record into ONE semicolon-delimited string: '8;Surf San Bernardino I-15 R21.71;;-117.47887;34.31525;3179;South;San Bernardino;I-15;;R;21.71;;' - with empty fields and a trailing delimiter. Positional parse, and it disagrees slightly with the station's own lat/lon.
essPrecipYesNo=2 means NO precipitation (1=precip, 2=no precip, 3=error). A truthy test on this field inverts the meaning.

sources.$seedReliabilityComment: Direct instrument readings from the operating agency - as high as NBI. The uncertainty here is whether a sensor EXISTS at a location, not whether it is telling the truth.

sources.$eventClassesComment: DELIBERATELY EMPTY. A camera is not an event. This is a VERIFICATION and enrichment source: it can attach a near-real-time image to a candidate produced by another feed, and (with vision) it could corroborate one - but it never originates a candidate on its own. If the vocabulary ever needs an entry for observational imagery, that is a schema change, not a value to invent here.
sources.$cadenceComment: The IMAGE refreshes on currentImageUpdateFrequency=3 minutes; the CATALOG JSON changes only when cameras are added or moved. Two different cadences in one source - poll the JSON rarely and the images often.
sources.$redistributableComment: Imagery raises a question the other feeds do not: republishing a live public-road camera frame. Confirm with Caltrans BEFORE any UI embeds it, separately from the data licence question.
sources.$snapshotComment: A camera leaving the list means it was decommissioned or taken out of service, not that anything on the road changed. Lifecycle barely applies - this is an inventory, like NBI.
sources.$statusComment: Same two blockers as ca-cwwp2-lcs. Additionally: only ONE camera on CA I-40, so the payoff here is a demo of image/vision enrichment, not corridor coverage.

notes: ONE camera on CA I-40: index 383, 'At Desert Oasis Rest Area', pm 28.475, inService=true. 503 cameras in D8 and exactly one on the corridor - D8's cameras are overwhelmingly urban (I-10/I-15/I-215/SR-91).

STILL IMAGES WORK, HLS MOSTLY DOES NOT. The I-40 JPEG returned HTTP 200, 60,809 bytes, 320x260, with an EXIF datetime of 2026:08:11 14:00:04 and Last-Modified 21:00:11 GMT - about 2 minutes old at fetch. Its advertised streamingVideoURL (wzmedia.dot.ca.gov/D8/LB-8_40_383.stream/playlist.m3u8) returned HTTP 404. Sampling three more D8 cameras: 1 of 3 playlists live, 2 of 3 404. So streamingVideoURL is ASPIRATIONAL METADATA - it must be probed per camera, never assumed.

FRESHNESS MUST NOT COME FROM recordTimestamp. That field is the camera's INVENTORY record date - 2025-07-03 for camera 1, 2025-01-21 for camera 40, i.e. over a year stale - while the image behind it is minutes old. Using recordTimestamp as observation time would age every frame by a year and trip every freshness alarm. Use the JPEG's HTTP Last-Modified (present) or its EXIF datetime.
The image itself carries provenance: JPEG comment 'County: SBD' plus an EXIF datetime. Cheaper and more trustworthy than the JSON for time.

Each camera advertises 12+ image URLs: currentImageURL plus referenceImage1..10UpdatesAgoURL, a rolling 15-minute-interval history. That is a FREE SHORT TIME SERIES per camera - the only source in this catalog offering look-back without storing it ourselves.
inService is the string 'true'/'false', not a boolean. cms uses capitalised 'True'/'False'. Same portal, two different boolean spellings.
location.route is the clean matchable field ('I-40'); locationName embeds the index and prose ('I-40 : (383) At Desert Oasis Rest Area').
Caltrans writes interstates as 'I-40' - matching this catalog's canonical form, unlike TxDOT's 'IH0040'. First source needing no route-name crosswalk.

sources.$seedReliabilityComment: Lowest in the catalog, and NOT a criticism of the camera. An image is ground truth about pixels; turning it into 'the right lane is blocked' takes an inference step no other source requires. The prior belongs to that inference, not to Caltrans.
sources.$independenceComment: SUBTLETY: a camera image is arguably the most independent evidence available - it is a direct observation, not a report. But it comes to us through the same D8 TMC as the LCS closure it would corroborate, and the CAMERA SITING is chosen by that TMC. Grouped with caltrans deliberately; revisit only with a real argument, not for convenience.

sources.$eventClassesComment: DELIBERATELY EMPTY, and this is the important one. A changeable message sign states what an operator DECIDED TO DISPLAY, which is neither an event nor located where the sign is - see the Jean, Nevada note in observed.notes. Treating sign text as an event report at the sign's coordinates manufactures phantom corridor events. Useful as CORROBORATING TEXT for a candidate located by another source, and as an operator-intent signal.
sources.$cadenceComment: recordTimestamp tracked wall clock to the minute across probes (13:58:47 then 13:59:47), so this is the FRESHEST feed in the catalog. Still ASSUMED rather than measured over a long window.
sources.$snapshotComment: display flipping to 'Blank' is an AFFIRMATIVE statement that the operator took the message down. Unlike the 511 feeds there is no ambiguity, because the sign is always present in the feed whether or not it is displaying - absence of a MESSAGE is reported explicitly rather than by the record disappearing. That is what makes this a clean 'cleared'.

notes: THE TRAP THAT MATTERS, VERIFIED LIVE: the I-40 sign at Barstow (pm 3, westbound) was displaying 'HWY-15 CLOSED / 15-N AT JEAN / USE ALT RTE'. Jean is in NEVADA, on I-15, roughly 150 miles from this sign and not on I-40 at all. Geocoding sign text to the sign's own coordinates would have created an I-40 Barstow closure that does not exist. The same message appeared on an SR-58 sign and three I-15 signs - one upstream event, five signs, zero of them at the event.
3 of 95 D8 signs are on I-40 (pm 3 x2 near Barstow, pm 149 near Needles). 2 of the 3 were Blank.

MESSAGE TEXT IS 3 LINES x 2 PHASES OF FIXED-WIDTH SIGN GLYPHS, not prose. Alignment is done with runs of spaces ('I-10L-202           9'), words are truncated to fit, and route names appear as 'HWY-15', '15-N', 'I-10L-202', 'CA-91' in the same feed. Any NLP over this must treat whitespace as layout, not as tokens.
33 of 95 signs displaying text; 62 Blank. display is '1 Page (Normal)' or 'Blank' - a prose enum with parentheses, not a code.

MOST LIVE TEXT IS TRAVEL TIMES, NOT INCIDENTS: 'MINUTES TO / I-210 10 MIN / Devore 16 MIN'. Roughly two thirds of displaying signs. These are useful as a congestion signal but are not events, and they are the reason a naive 'sign has text -> something is wrong' rule is mostly false positives.

Genuine incident text does appear and is specific: '15 N NEAR PRIMM / LANES STOPPED / EXPECT DELAYS' and '15-N /CANTU / GALLEANO / 2 RT LNS CLOSED' - the latter carries a lane count no other CA feed states in structured form.
messageTimestamp CAN BE MONTHS OLD ON A BLANK SIGN (2025-10-21 on the Needles sign) while recordTimestamp is current. On a Blank sign the message timestamp refers to the last message, not to now.
inService is the string 'True'/'False' (capitalised) here, but 'true'/'false' in cctv and lcs. Same portal, inconsistent booleans.
location.route is populated and clean ('I-40'), so sign LOCATION is reliable even though sign CONTENT is not locatable.

sources.$seedReliabilityComment: The sign is a fact; what it implies about the corridor is not. Low because content is unlocatable and often a travel time rather than an event - and because an operator leaving a stale message up is a known failure mode this feed cannot distinguish from a current one.

sources.$authComment: Fully public, no key. This is the machine-readable backing feed for the cad.chp.ca.gov/Traffic.aspx page - that page is HTML with a 60-second meta-refresh and should NOT be scraped when this XML exists. Verified live 2026-08-11.
sources.$cadenceComment: The HTML page self-refreshes every 60s, and observed detail entries were ~1 minute old. ASSUMED from those two signals, not measured.
sources.license: unknown - CHP publishes this publicly but states no terms
sources.$redistributableComment: Raises a PRIVACY question the DOT feeds do not. Dispatch narrative is written by officers for officers and can contain vehicle descriptions, plate fragments, and injury detail. Even if redistribution is permitted, republishing IncidentDetail verbatim is a separate decision from republishing that an incident exists.
sources.$snapshotComment: This is a live dispatch board: a log leaves the feed when the incident is closed out. Closer to 'cleared' than the 511 feeds - BUT clearance here means CHP closed the CAD log, which can precede the road actually being clear. Confirm with CHP; until then treat disappearance as 'clearing' for closures even though this field says cleared.
sources.$statusComment: URL verified working; no adapter, and CA is outside the current corridor definition. Note this is CA-ONLY - it does not help AZ/NM/TX/OK.

notes: STATEWIDE SNAPSHOT IS SMALL AND CURRENT: 199 active logs across 4 centers (SAHB, GGHB, LAHB, INHB) and 23 dispatches. This is active incidents only, not a day's history - so it is a genuine real-time feed, and backfill is impossible from it.
ONE I-40 record at probe time: a WIND Advisory at 'I40 E / Fort Cady Rd Ofr', Barstow area. Low volume on this corridor is expected - CA I-40 is ~155 rural miles.

EVERY TEXT VALUE IS WRAPPED IN LITERAL DOUBLE-QUOTE CHARACTERS INSIDE THE XML ELEMENT: <LogTime>"Aug 11 2026  1:55PM"</LogTime>. The quotes are part of the text node. A standard XML parse yields '"Aug 11 2026  1:55PM"' with quotes attached - they must be stripped explicitly, and an empty field is the two-character string '""', not ''.

LATLON PACKS TWO INTEGERS AND OMITS THE LONGITUDE SIGN: '34817195:116615860' means 34.817195, -116.615860. The minus is IMPLICIT (all of California is west). Decoding naively gives +116, which lands in China. Divide by 1e6 and negate the second value. Present on 199 of 199 - no nulls.

TIMESTAMPS ARE HUMAN PROSE WITH NO TIMEZONE AND DOUBLE-SPACED HOURS: 'Aug 11 2026  1:55PM'. No offset, no zone abbreviation, 12-hour clock, and two spaces before a single-digit hour. Assume America/Los_Angeles and expect DST ambiguity twice a year.

LogType IS A CHP RADIO CODE PLUS A LABEL: '1125-Traffic Hazard', '1179-Trfc Collision-1141 Enrt', '20002-Hit and Run No Injuries', 'CLOSURE of a Road', 'MZP-Assist CT with Maintenance', 'SIG Alert', 'WIND Advisory'. Mixed numeric-code and alpha-code namespaces in one field. 'CLOSURE of a Road' (9 observed) is the class-3 signal; '11xx' codes are collisions; 'MZP' (67 observed, the single most common type) is CHP assisting Caltrans maintenance - which is a WORK ZONE indicator, not an incident.

Location vs LocationDesc are BOTH freeform and inconsistent: 'I40 E / Fort Cady Rd Ofr' with LocationDesc 'EO'. Route is written 'I40' and 'I15' (no hyphen) here, but 'I-40' in the Caltrans feeds - a crosswalk is required within California.

LogDetails is a nested list of timestamped narrative lines prefixed with a priority in brackets: '[3] RP ADV LUMBER IS SPLINTERING...'. Heavy abbreviation (RP = reporting party, ADV = advises, VEHS = vehicles, RHS = right hand shoulder, #1 = lane 1). This is the richest LANE-LEVEL prose in any source, and it is officer shorthand, not English.

Area is a CHP beat name, not a road or a county: 'Barstow', 'Needles' was absent at probe time, 'Victorville', 'Morongo Basin'. 90 distinct values including bare two-letter codes ('BC', 'FR1', 'TK') - so Area is a WEAK geographic filter and LATLON is the reliable one.
Only 4 Center elements appear, not all CHP divisions - centers with no active logs are omitted entirely rather than appearing empty.

sources.$seedReliabilityComment: First-responder dispatch, so an incident report is about as authoritative as it gets for 'something is happening now' - above the 511 feeds. NOT higher, because CAD logs are opened on unverified public reports ('RP ADV...') and the feed does not distinguish a confirmed incident from a caller's claim.
sources.$independenceComment: CHP is a genuinely separate agency from Caltrans with its own dispatch system, so chp-cad CAN corroborate ca-cwwp2-lcs - one of the few real independent pairs in this catalog. CAVEAT: 'MZP-Assist CT with Maintenance' logs exist BECAUSE Caltrans requested assistance, so for work zones specifically the two are correlated. Independence is per-class here, which the single-group model cannot express - see weathershare-oss for the same problem in a worse form.

sources.$endpointComment: ONE concrete dataset, deliberately. The portal serves six (RWIS/OSS_rwis, CCTV/OSS_cctv, CMS/OSS_cms, INCIDENTS/OSS_incidents, ROADINFO/OSS_roadinfo, CHAIN/OSS_chain), all verified live 2026-08-11. A {DATASET} template here would be unschedulable - ingest-stack.ts correctly refuses to poll a template - and would also imply one independence group across six datasets. See $independenceComment.
sources.$authComment: Fully public. No key, no registration. Verified live 2026-08-11. THIS IS THE POINT OF THE SOURCE: New Mexico with no credential and no agency negotiation.
sources.$specComment: WORST CASE IN THE CATALOG: undocumented AND the schema VARIES BY UPSTREAM WITHIN A SINGLE FILE. A Caltrans roadinfo record and an NMDOT roadinfo record share almost no field names. This string is OUR label for the NMDOT property set observed live.
sources.$mappingIssueComment: Highest mapping-issue count a HEALTHY run produces. MEASURED 2026-08-13..17: flat at 7 across 684 runs. Unmappable values are recorded rather than dropped, so a steady rate is correct behaviour and only a spike means the format drifted. Drives the per-source CorridorEventHub-mapping-issue-spike-* alarm threshold; raise it if this feed legitimately gets noisier.
sources.$cadenceComment: ASSUMED. The `updated` field ('YYYYMMDDHHMM UTC' - the only source in this catalog that states its own zone in the value) was BYTE-IDENTICAL across all 84 NMDOT records, so it is the aggregator's scrape time and cadence must be derived by diffing fetches, not read off a record.
sources.$cadenceMeasured: MEASURED 2026-08-12 over 226 fetches / 18.7h, and this is the ONE source where the measurement worked: 113 distinct payloads out of 226 fetches, so the real refresh is ~600s. It is the only source in the catalog that embeds NO per-request timestamp, which is precisely why the duplicates are visible here and invisible everywhere else - all 107 duplicate-checksum pairs in the raw zone were this feed. CHANGED 300 -> 600 on the strength of that measurement: we were fetching and storing a 4MB payload twice per refresh. Worst-case staleness goes 300s -> 600s against a 1800s freshnessSlo, and the 30-minute staleness alarm still gets three collections per window.
sources.license: unknown - aggregator terms unstated AND NMDOT terms unconfirmed
sources.$redistributableComment: TWO permissions are needed, not one: an aggregator cannot grant rights its upstream did not. Confirm with BOTH the Western States Forum (aggregator) and NMDOT (originator) before the public API exposes this. Scoping the adapter to a single upstream at least makes that a two-party question instead of an eight-party one.
sources.$snapshotComment: OPEN QUESTION 2, and STRICTLY WORSE HERE THAN FOR A DIRECT FEED. A record disappearing may mean the event cleared, NMDOT dropped it, or the aggregator's scrape of NMDOT failed - and nothing in the payload distinguishes the third case from the first two. Disappearance MUST route to `clearing`, never `cleared` (ADR 0003). Ask NMDOT; the aggregator cannot answer it.
sources.$statusComment: Scheduled. Endpoint is concrete (no template), the adapter exists (adapters/nm_dot_weathershare.py), and it is a poll rather than a batch - so it satisfies both guards in ingest-stack.ts and the drift tests in tests/test_config.py.

notes: WHY THIS SOURCE EXISTS: New Mexico was the one corridor state with NO working feed - nm-dot-wzdx has been returning 503. 84 live NMDOT records here, 2 on I-40, no credential required.

THE FILE IS 8 AGENCIES IN ONE: 2,499 CALTRANS, 2,064 AZDOT, 250 MDOT, 216 WSDOT, 154 OregonDOT, 84 NMDOT, 76 UDOT, 64 NDOT. The adapter reads ONLY source=='NMDOT' - see $independenceComment for why that is a correctness requirement rather than scope reduction.
DOUBLE-WRAPPED ROOT: the JSON root is an array of length 1 whose single element is the actual record array - [[{...},{...}]]. Reading root[0] as a record yields a list.

NMDOT VALUES ARE [FIELDNAME, VALUE] PAIRS: "routeNumber": ["routeNumber", "40"], "eventType": ["eventType", 8]. The key is repeated inside its own value, on 5 of 14 fields (routeName, routeNumber, eventType, description) and NOT on the other 9. str() of the 2-list looks almost plausible in a log.

THERE IS NO RECORD ID. No id, uid, log-id, or index on any of the 84 records - the only source in this catalog with nothing to put in SourceRef.native_id. The adapter synthesizes one from route + title + coordinates rounded to 4dp, deliberately EXCLUDING the description body (which is edited as conditions change) and `updated` (which changes every scrape). A title edit still mints a new id, so the matcher's spatial overlap has to absorb it. Ask NMDOT for an id.

THERE ARE NO EVENT TIMES. starttime and endtime are the EMPTY STRING on all 84 records. start_time falls back to retrieved_at with time_confidence 'estimated', end_time is open-ended, and both are reported as mapping issues per record so a fetch time is never mistaken for an agency-stated one.
ROUTE IS SPLIT ACROSS TWO FIELDS and never written as 'I-40': routeName 'I' + routeNumber '40'. routeName observed: NM(33), US(22), NA(16), I(12), null(1).

PROSE MATCHING WOULD BE WRONG, AND DANGEROUSLY SO. 5 NMDOT records mention I-40 in their text; only 2 are ON I-40. Two are NM 566 records naming I-40 as a landmark ('at mile marker 0, Church Rock (I-40)'). The third is a genuine height restriction - 'Low Clearance Structure, CMV's please use I-40 between exits 89 & 96. Height Restriction 13'6"' - which RECOMMENDS I-40 as the truck detour. A prose match would place a 13'6" clearance limit ON the corridor it tells trucks to use: the exact inversion of the fact, on the class where being wrong strands a truck under a bridge. The adapter matches on routeName+routeNumber structurally.

eventType IS AN UNDOCUMENTED NUMERIC ENUM. Correlated 1:1 against rendered titles across all 84 records with no crossover: 5=Closure(3), 7=Alert(16), 8=Lane Closure(4), 9=Roadwork(33), 13=Fair Driving Conditions(13), 16=Difficult Driving Conditions(12), 19=?(1), 20=Seasonal Closure(2). Strong evidence, still inference.

eventType 7 AND 19 ARE DELIBERATELY UNMAPPED - 17 of 84 records quarantined rather than guessed. 'Alert' is a container word spanning dimensional_restriction (the height restriction above), a truck-length prohibition, and general advisories with no class at all. 19 has n=1. Ask NMDOT for the enum; this is the single biggest data-yield question on this source.

REAL AGENCY ROAD-SURFACE REPORTS: eventType 13/16 are 'Fair Driving Conditions - Roads are wet' and 'Difficult Driving Conditions', 25 of 84 records. Class 6 everywhere else in this catalog is DERIVED (NWS alerts) or absent (Caltrans put no pavement sensors on I-40). None of the 25 were on I-40 at probe time, but the class is genuinely sourced rather than inferred.

MILEPOST RANGES IN PROSE on 52 of 84 records ('from mile marker 344, 8 miles east of Tucumcari to mile marker 350'), points on 15 ('at mile marker 164'), neither on 17. This is the only NM source giving a LINEAR extent. The adapter cross-checks the parsed milepost against the record's own coordinate and reports a disagreement rather than silently preferring one - two independent position statements in one record is an error-detection opportunity.

DIRECTION IS PROSE-ONLY AND USUALLY ABSENT: only 10 of 84 records contain any bound word, so UNKNOWN is the normal case. The observed I-40 lane closure says 'northbound and eastbound' - a contradiction on an east-west corridor. North/south are reported as issues, not coerced.
The description '~~~' delimiter separates title from body; some records carry no delimiter and are title-only. One record's name is the degenerate 'Alert, Alert'.

ODOT IN THIS FILE MEANS OREGON, not Oklahoma - a direct collision with this project's ok-odot-wzdx. Agency spelling is also inconsistent across datasets: AZDOT here vs ADOT in cms, CALTRANS here vs Caltrans in cms vs 'California Department of Transportation' in cctv.

2,064 AZDOT RECORDS ARE EMPTY SHELLS - every one carries only {source, typeabbr, starttime:'', endtime:'', updated:null}. 38% of the file and ZERO usable AZ records. A record count is not a data count, and this is the clearest example of that in the catalog. AZ is covered by az511-events regardless.

OTHER DATASETS ON THIS PORTAL, NOT WIRED IN: cctv (19,850 cameras, 40 on I-40 across all states - the best imagery target found so far), cms (290 ADOT + 134 NMDOT signs), incidents (209 CHP, same data as chp-cad with coordinates already decoded), rwis (392 stations, none on I-40, and it independently CONFIRMS our NTCIP decoding: 100.58 F / 11.18 mph / 20.67 mi where raw Caltrans reads 381 / 50 / 332700).

sources.$seedReliabilityComment: BELOW every direct DOT feed in this catalog (OK/TX/AZ at 0.8, Caltrans 0.85) on purpose. An aggregator cannot be more reliable than its upstream, and it adds scrape lag plus a transformation step that demonstrably loses data - the 2,064 empty AZDOT records are the proof, in this very file. If nm-dot-wzdx comes back up, prefer it and drop this to a corroborator.
sources.$independenceComment: 'nmdot', NOT 'aggregator-oss', and that is only true BECAUSE the adapter filters to a single upstream. THE GENERAL PROBLEM IS REAL AND UNSOLVED: this endpoint re-serves Caltrans, ADOT, NMDOT, CHP, UDOT, NDOT, OregonDOT and WSDOT simultaneously, so an adapter reading all of them would need a group that is correct for none - and a re-served ADOT closure would corroborate THE SAME closure from az511-events, inflating confidence exactly where the independence grouping exists to prevent it. Reading the other upstreams requires independenceGroup to become PER-CANDIDATE rather than per-source, which is a schema change. Scoping to one upstream buys correctness today without pretending the model is adequate.
sources.$relatedSourceWarning: LATENT BUG, recorded rather than silently fixed: nm-dot-wzdx carries independenceGroup 'blyncsy' (the vendor hosting it), but its DATA is also NMDOT's. If that feed returns, it and this source would look independent and corroborate each other - two routes to one agency's report, which is exactly the aws-location-traffic/HERE situation. Harmless only because nm-dot-wzdx is endpoint_down with no adapter. Move it to 'nmdot' before reviving it.

$missingComment: NOT COVERED by any open feed: incidents and closures (classes 2-3), congestion (4), bridge clearance (7). Probed oktraffic.org for /incidents, /events, /restarea, /trafficspeed, /dms — all 404. Incidents are the most fragmented class across agencies and the one with the highest duplicate rate, so they REQUIRE DOT agreements, and no amount of engineering shortens that.
$reliabilityComment: SeedReliability is a SEED PRIOR only - a hand-guessed starting value, to be REPLACED by scores computed from observed outcomes (false-positive rate, clear-time accuracy, location error, staleness). independenceGroup matters for corroboration: sources sharing a group are counted ONCE for corroboration, because two feeds reselling the same upstream are not independent evidence. Both live here rather than in corridor_event_hub/core because core must never name a specific source.
